_notes: VerificationAgent.verify_insights() (agents/verification/agent.py) also calls an LLM (settings.verifier_model, default 'gpt-4o') to decompose each DraftInsight into atomic assertions and check each against its cited evidence, so -- like the reasoning stage -- this cannot be hand-derived from purely deterministic code the way stages 1-4 were.

What IS deterministic given a stubbed verifier LLM response: verification_confidence = round(coverage * avg_verified_confidence, 4) where coverage = verified_count/total_count; verification_status is 'flagged' if any contradiction OR not all assertions verified OR confidence < 0.75, else 'auto_verified'; requires_clinician_review is True whenever status != 'auto_verified' OR severity is 'high'/'critical' (always True for high/critical regardless of verification outcome) -- see agent.py lines ~195-210. This fixture assumes every atomic assertion below the mock verifier returns is verified with no contradictions, which is the expected outcome given how directly each assertion is supported by 05_expected_normalized_entities.json and 07_expected_knowledge_topics.json.

This fixture consumes expected_draft_insight_set from 08_expected_reasoning_insights.json as its DraftInsightSet input -- draft-001 (HbA1c, moderate), draft-002 (CKD pattern, high), draft-003 (lipid panel, moderate).
